implemented_requirements.evidence: Board class defined with self.grid initialized to starting position in board.py

implemented_requirements.requirement: Move representation (start/end, promotion, castling flags, etc.)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Move class with appropriate fields defined in move.py

implemented_requirements.requirement: Legal move generation (including pawn moves, captures, castling, en‑passant, promotion)
implemented_requirements.evidence: No method in Board for generating or validating moves is present in the provided files.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Applying a move to the board and updating state (board, castling rights, en‑passant, half‑move clock, full‑move number)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board class lacks any method that mutates the board based on a Move.
No code for attack detection, check evaluation, or game‑end conditions is provided.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Terminal rendering of the board after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board class does not contain a __str__ or render method; no printing logic is shown.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Parsing of standard algebraic notation (e.g., Ke8, O-O, e8=Q)
implemented_requirements.evidence: notation.py only contains a stub function header; no parsing implementation.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Main game loop that reads player input, validates, updates board, and announces winner
implemented_requirements.evidence: No script or function implementing a game loop is present.

critical_issues: Missing move generation and validation logic; the engine cannot determine legal moves.
No implementation of check, check‑mate, or stalemate detection, so winner cannot be determined.
No terminal UI or input parsing; the program cannot be played from the Linux terminal.
Board class lacks methods to render the board, apply moves, or update game state.
Incomplete Move __repr__ and missing utility functions make debugging impossible.
judge.summary: The repository contains only skeletal data structures (Board, Move, Piece) and a few constants. Core functionality required for a playable terminal chess game—move generation, rule enforcement (castling, en passant, promotion), check/checkmate detection, input parsing, board rendering, and a game loop—is absent. Consequently, the solution does not meet the benchmark requirements and is unlikely to be executable.
